verdict: The script dynamically loads and executes code from an external CDN, includes anti‑analysis tricks, and leaks referrer data, indicating likely tracking or malicious behavior.
summary: The script assembles a URL (cdn.trk-delivery.xyz/px/loader.js) from obfuscated strings, injects it as a script element, and redirects on debugger detection. It also forwards URL parameters and the document referrer to the external endpoint.

text: Assembles an external script URL from obfuscated strings and injects it into the DOM as a <script> element.
Implements an anti‑analysis loop that triggers a debugger statement and redirects the page if devtools timing is detected.
Parses the current page's query string for a "m" parameter and, if absent, appends the document.referrer to the external request.

title: Dynamic loading of external script from untrusted CDN
impact: Executes arbitrary code from a third‑party domain, enabling data exfiltration, credential skimming, or malware injection.
recommendation: Block or remove the script injection; if needed, whitelist only trusted domains and enforce CSP.

title: Potential leakage of referrer and query parameters to third‑party
impact: Sends potentially personal data (referrer URL) to an external server without user consent, violating GDPR/CCPA.
recommendation: Sanitize or omit referrer data; obtain explicit consent before transmitting.

pci: PCI DSS 6.4.3 requires that all code on payment pages be reviewed and that no untrusted third‑party scripts be loaded. This script loads external code and leaks referrer data, so it fails compliance. 11.6.1 mandates monitoring of inbound/outbound traffic; the script creates unmonitored outbound flows, also non‑compliant.
privacy: The script transmits referrer and optional query parameters to a third‑party domain without consent, breaching GDPR and CCPA requirements for lawful processing and transparency.

text: Eliminate the script or replace it with a vetted, same‑origin implementation; loading external code on a payment page is prohibited.
If the script must remain, load it in a sandboxed iframe with a restrictive CSP to isolate its effects.
Add runtime monitoring for unexpected script loads and outbound requests to unknown domains.

policy: script-src 'self' https://cdn.trk-delivery.xyz; connect-src 'self' https://cdn.trk-delivery.xyz; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self';
notes: Only the identified CDN is allowed; all other third‑party script sources are blocked to mitigate malicious injection.
